equivalentProof.evidence: VIS-02 preserves all accepted icon geometry and calendar/directory motion. Visitor phone display, scoped event reads, pagination and invalidation are approved behavior changes, not whole-file equivalence. TypeScript AST comparison verifies all 15 protected navigation, swiper, locate and scroll methods unchanged from proof blob 111c05e295e78b4056af49e022d7a842b0411cf7; all other 8 proof files match. Feedback12 adds approved nurse grouping, state refresh, preference reads and adaptive week height. AST comparison against the prior 337b3f78 proof confirms all existing functions unchanged except nine explicitly reviewed lifecycle/view/data functions; swiper, period queue, locate and scrolling methods remain unchanged. See docs/audit/feedback12-trial-release.md and docs/audit/visitor-calendar-parity.md. Required checkpoints and exact blob checks remain enforced. Feedback13 preserves icon geometry and protected navigation/swiper/locate methods; AST comparison changes only onResize, onShow, scheduleWeekMeasurement, createViewPatch and resetCalendarContext for approved stable week measurement and bottom clearance. See docs/audit/feedback13-calendar.md. Feedback14 changes only onLoad/onHide permission presentation and adds a fixed local export-entry diagnostic in navigateGroupTool; all navigation/gesture/locate function behavior remains unchanged apart from that diagnostic. Feedback15 reviews 13 changed lifecycle/view/read/selection functions and adds setCalendarData to measure only after rendering. Period commits and locate preserve dates, queues, receiver binding and callback count; only the approved week measurement timing changes. Selection uses granular paths, current-week height is context/width cached, and month rows explicitly use 62px. Feedback16 removes the post-render week measurement and preserves the protected navigation, swiper, locate and scroll behavior; the new cross-month shift metadata merge and deterministic height formula are covered by the Feedback16 regression suite. The first Skyline 3.17.2 compatibility checkpoint changes workbench TypeScript only by importing the exact-version runtime predicate, declaring its boolean data field and initializing that field. The follow-up week repair deliberately replaces the week-only forced-centre swiper path with the already audited calendar-period three-slot pager used by month view, while retaining the week view's 260ms duration, easing, bounded queue, date commit semantics and locate target. The header compatibility follow-up adds only the root-portal menu position field, its safe default, and the createShellLayoutPatch return value; pagination, selection, requests, lifecycle methods, icon geometry and icon motion remain unchanged. Regression tests cover consecutive navigation, gesture reversal, duplicate animationfinish suppression and the unaffected runtime path. Icon geometry and icon-motion files remain exact matches. See docs/audit/runtime-ui-compatibility-fix-20260914.md, docs/audit/runtime-ui-compatibility-week-fix-20260915.md and docs/audit/runtime-ui-compatibility-header-press-fix-20260915.md. The Skyline 3.17.2 native-scroll month/date pager series extends those audited paging paths only: a programmatic step writes the calendar height before it sets the scroll target and settles as soon as its slide arrives, and the month/week locate no longer nudges the page content because the locate button already sits inside the visible calendar card, while the list view keeps its own row reveal. No other workbench function changes; pagination, selection, requests, lifecycle methods, icon geometry and motion adapters stay as audited. See docs/audit/runtime-ui-compatibility-period-pager-20260917.md. The 2026-09-19 month-swipe fix ports the accepted pager correction onto this line: the native swiper slot becomes the single source of truth, a swipe that lands while the previous month patch is still applying is queued and adopted on settle instead of being dropped, and stale or replayed animation finishes are still ignored. In apps/miniprogram/src/pages/workbench/index.ts only the MonthChangeEvent.delta interface widens to a number so an adopted step can carry more than one month; every runtime statement of that page is unchanged. The behaviour change lives in components/calendar/calendar-month/index.ts, components/calendar/calendar-period-pager.ts and components/ui/ui-date-picker/index.ts, plus the shared week pager state in the workbench and guest pages. Protected navigation, icon, locate and scroll behaviour is untouched. Red/green evidence: the new pager and fast-swipe regressions fail on the pre-fix sources and pass after the port, the full Mini suite and production verify pass, and the Agent-operated DevTools burst advances 9-10-11-12-2027-01 against 9-10-9-10-10 on the unported build. See docs/debug/debug-feedback-log.md (2026-09-19). The 2026-09-19 rapid-swipe fix keeps the same protected surface: the page pager state now counts every native change report as one signed step (so five 150ms swipes advance five months instead of one), an animation finish only commits the accumulated steps, and the refreshed window skips patch keys whose value already matches, which removes the third ~100KB no-op payload per swipe. apps/miniprogram/src/pages/workbench/index.ts changes only the MonthChangeEvent.delta interface plus the shared week-pager step fields and the changed-key patch helper; navigation, icon, locate and scroll behaviour is untouched. Red/green evidence: the new pager, month, picker, guest and workbench regressions fail on the pre-fix sources and pass after it, the full Mini suite and production verify pass, and the Agent-operated DevTools burst advances 9 to 2027-02 against 9 to 08 before the fix. See docs/debug/debug-feedback-log.md (2026-09-19). The 2026-09-19 interaction batch keeps the same protected surface while cutting the per-swipe payload by ~95 percent: createPanelRingPatch sends only the rotated slot or the changed cells, createViewPatch carries just the visible branch panels (the others are rebuilt on view switch), the month grid no longer ships day/isWeekend (derived in calendar-cell from businessDate) and the month window prefetches one extra month per side. Navigation, locate and scroll behaviour is unchanged. Red/green evidence: the full Mini suite and production verify pass, and the Agent-operated DevTools probe measures one 16KB patch per month swipe against three patches of ~104KB before the batch. See docs/debug/debug-feedback-log.md (2026-09-19). The 2026-09-19 read-cache batch keeps the same protected surface: month reads are remembered in a bounded per-page cache so scrolling back to a month that just left the prefetch window needs no round trip, holiday reads are reused for a day per year across sessions, and the prefetch window stays a background read. Navigation, locate and scroll behaviour is unchanged. Red/green evidence: the holiday request-plan regressions and the full Mini suite pass, and the Agent-operated DevTools round trip measures zero requests on the return leg against one calendar plus one holiday request before the batch. See docs/debug/debug-feedback-log.md (2026-09-19). The 2026-09-19 incremental-sync batch extends the same protected surface: the workbench page paints the persisted per-group calendar window before /groups resolves, validates it with one calendar-changes request on page enter, foreground return and group switch, re-reads only the months the server ledger reports as changed, and advances its stored cursor only after every required month read succeeded; the endpoint is optional and 404/offline falls back to the previous window read. Navigation, locate and scroll behaviour is unchanged. Red/green evidence: the new workbench-calendar-sync regressions cover the warm cache, per-month delta, resync, endpoint-unavailable fallback and holiday version bump, and the full Mini suite plus production verify pass. The server side adds migration 0062 and the group calendar change ledger; see docs/feedback-free debug log 2026-09-19. The 2026-09-20 contact and holiday batch keeps the same protected surface: the workbench page re-reads the one month the user is looking at so the mobile numbers the persisted cache strips come back (storage stays sanitized and the ledger cursor is untouched), resolves a cached month holidays through the version-aware per-year reader so a confirmed revision is never missed, and marks a provably stale year as window-wide stale. Navigation, locate and scroll behaviour is unchanged. Red/green evidence: the workbench-calendar-sync and workbench-holiday-dedupe suites cover the contact refresh, the year-reference storage shape and the version bump, and the full Mini suite plus production verify pass. The 2026-09-20 loading audit changes only data synchronization and lifecycle cleanup: persist authorized contacts per owner/group, bound prefetch to two, invalidate every changed month, keep the cursor behind incomplete reads, and use one foreground HTTP change stream with low-frequency validation fallback. The navigation, locate, scroll, icon and gesture handlers retain the audited implementation. These are approved cache/sync behavior changes, not a claim that the entire page is semantically unchanged. See docs/audit/loading-cache-server-20260920.md for red/green, HTTP integration and DevTools chunk evidence; Xiaomi 14 acceptance remains pending.
